title: The Book of Filial Duty
dateDisplay: c. 3rd–2nd centuries BCE, with later tales
attributionNote: The classic of filial piety is a composite treatise of the Warring States or early Han, traditionally ascribed to Zengzi; the twenty-four tales that follow it are later moral exempla, edited with the text in this edition.
description: Ivan Chen's translation of the Classic of Filial Piety, with the twenty-four examples of filial children that Chinese primers attached to it: the emperor who tasted his mother's medicine, the son who carried rice for his parents over a hundred li, the children who warmed the bed or exposed themselves to mosquitoes for their elders. The tales carry the treatise's ethics into the household and show how it was taught.
historicalContext: The Hsiao Ching's eighteen chapters circulated with a commentary by the Tang emperor Xuanzong and were used to teach the duty of children to parents and subjects to rulers. The twenty-four examples form a separate popular tradition that was bound with the classic in village schools; Chen's English version, with the Chinese text, was printed in London in 1908.
availabilityNote: Complete: the classic's eighteen chapters and the twenty-four examples, streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter or tale per page. The editorial note and the translator's introduction are volume apparatus and are not part of the work.
